whyZincPage.heading: Why choose zinc die-casting?
whyZincPage.heroImageAlt: Two zinc die-cast components showing chrome-plated and powder-coated surface finishes
whyZincPage.intro:
Zinc die-casting is an efficient and cost-effective solution for technical components that demand high precision, strength and attractive surface finishes. At Linimatic we produce zinc parts both small and large — from just a few grams up to 4 kg.

Compared to aluminum die-casting, zinc offers shorter cycle times, lower energy consumption, and significantly longer tool life. Altogether, this often means lower production costs per part — especially for larger series and parts with a favorable material weight.

Zinc's excellent flow properties also make it possible to cast complex geometries, thin wall thicknesses, fine detail and tight tolerances. This reduces the need for CNC machining and other post-processing, further contributing to a competitive price on the finished part.

advantages.title: Lower production costs
advantages.description: Short cycle times and an efficient casting process can result in a lower price per part — especially in larger production series.

advantages.title: Complex geometries
advantages.description: Zinc's excellent flow properties make it possible to die-cast advanced shapes, fine details, and integrated features into a single component.

advantages.title: Tight tolerances
advantages.description: Zinc die-casting provides high dimensional accuracy and good dimensional stability, reducing the need for subsequent machining.

advantages.title: Thin wall thicknesses
advantages.description: Zinc can fill very narrow sections of the mould, making it well suited for components with thin walls and fine details.

advantages.title: High strength and stiffness
advantages.description: Zinc alloys combine high mechanical strength with good stiffness and are well suited for load-bearing technical components.

advantages.title: Long tool life
advantages.description: Zinc's low melting temperature puts less stress on the mould than aluminum, often resulting in significantly longer tool life. As the tooling cost is amortized over more parts produced, it results in a lower tooling cost per part.

advantages.title: Attractive surfaces
advantages.description: Zinc produces a smooth, uniform as-cast surface suited for both visible components and subsequent surface treatment.

advantages.title: Fewer parts and process steps
advantages.description: Threads, ribs, bosses, logos and other features can often be integrated directly into the casting. This can reduce the number of components and assembly operations.

advantages.title: Effective electromagnetic shielding
advantages.description: Zinc is electrically conductive and can be used for housings and components that need to shield electronics from electromagnetic interference.

advantages.title: A recyclable material
advantages.description: Zinc can be recycled again and again without losing its fundamental properties. Production scrap can be remelted and returned to the material cycle.

comparison.heading: Zinc vs. the alternatives
comparison.description: Side-by-side comparison of zinc die-casting against aluminum, magnesium, and plastic injection moulding. The data explains why zinc wins when precision, surface quality, and tool economics are the deciding factors.

alloys.description: Zamak alloys are zinc-aluminium alloys optimised for die-casting. The right alloy depends on your part’s mechanical requirements, surface finish needs, and casting complexity. We cast all four standard grades and advise on selection during DFM review.

rows.name: Zamak 2

rows.name: Zamak 3

items.question: What is zinc die-casting?
items.answer: Zinc die-casting is a manufacturing process where molten zinc alloy is injected under high pressure into a steel die. The hot-chamber process keeps the alloy molten inside the machine, enabling cycle times as fast as 5–6 seconds. The result is a net-shape metal component with tight tolerances, excellent surface finish, and high repeatability — suitable for production volumes from hundreds to millions of parts.

items.question: What is a Zamak alloy?
items.answer: Zamak is a family of zinc-aluminium alloys specifically developed for die-casting. The name comes from the German abbreviations of its constituents: Zink, Aluminium, Magnesium, and Kupfer (copper). The four standard grades — Zamak 2, 3, 5, and 8 — offer different balances of strength, ductility, and castability. Zamak 3 is the most widely used, while Zamak 2 provides the highest strength.

items.question: What is the difference between zinc and Zamak?
items.answer: Zinc is the base element. Zamak is a specific family of zinc alloys engineered for die-casting, containing precisely controlled amounts of aluminium (3.5–4.3%), magnesium, and in some grades, copper. Pure zinc is too soft for most engineering applications — the alloying elements in Zamak provide the strength, hardness, and castability that make precision die-casting possible.

items.question: Is zinc die-casting stronger than aluminium?
items.answer: Yes, in terms of tensile strength. Zamak alloys range from 283 to 397 MPa, while most die-cast aluminium alloys deliver 150–300 MPa. Zinc also achieves tighter as-cast tolerances (±0.05 mm vs. ±0.1 mm) and produces chrome-ready surfaces without secondary polishing. However, aluminium is lighter (2.7 g/cm³ vs. 6.6 g/cm³), so the choice depends on whether strength-to-weight ratio or absolute precision is the priority.

items.question: Why not choose magnesium instead of zinc?
items.answer: Magnesium is the lightest of the three metals — lighter even than aluminium. However, zinc dies typically last over 1 million shots versus magnesium’s 200,000–300,000, tolerances are tighter (±0.05 mm vs. ±0.08 mm), and the strongest Zamak alloys exceed magnesium’s tensile strength (up to 397 MPa vs. 200–250 MPa). Magnesium can be the right choice when weight is the overriding factor — for most engineering parts, zinc offers better tooling economics, precision, and strength.

items.question: Can zinc die-cast parts be chrome plated?
items.answer: Yes, and this is one of zinc’s strongest advantages. Zinc die-castings have a smooth, consistent surface straight from the die, giving an excellent starting point for chrome plating. The surface must still be polished before plating to achieve a flawless, mirror-bright result. This makes zinc the preferred material for visible, decorative components in furniture, lighting, and consumer products where a flawless chrome finish is mandatory.

items.question: Do zinc die-cast parts corrode without surface treatment?
items.answer: Untreated zinc has good natural corrosion resistance and can often be used without surface treatment for indoor or hidden components. For outdoor use, humid environments, or where appearance and wear resistance matter, we offer a wide range of surface treatments — we help select the right option based on the part’s application.

items.question: What industries use zinc die-casting?
items.answer: Zinc die-cast components are delivered to a wide range of segments: industrial equipment, automotive, telecommunications, camera housings, and furniture and design products. What these customers share is a need for high precision, complex geometry, and reliable quality — across both small and large production runs.

items.question: Is zinc die-casting environmentally friendly?
items.answer: Zinc is 100% recyclable with no degradation of material properties. Its lower melting point (385°C vs. 660°C for aluminium) means less energy per casting cycle. At Linimatic, virtually all casting scrap — runners, overflows, and reject parts — is remelted and reused directly in production. We also offer lead-free zinc alloys through our Zinkers product line.

items.question: How much does zinc die-casting cost?
items.answer: Tooling cost depends on part complexity and number of cavities, typically ranging from €10,000 to €80,000. However, zinc dies last over 1 million shots — 5–10× longer than aluminium dies — dramatically reducing per-part tooling cost at volume. Piece prices depend on part weight, alloy, cycle time, and secondary operations. Send us your drawing for a specific quote — we respond within 48 hours.

aboutPage.heading: Denmark’s largest dedicated zinc die-casting foundry.
story: Linimatic is a Danish zinc die-casting foundry specialising in high-pressure die casting of zinc parts for industry. Since 1967 we have produced components in zinc in Helsinge, Denmark, with a focus on complex geometry, tight tolerances, high finish and stable quality.

As Denmark's largest dedicated zinc die-casting foundry, we help companies across Denmark and Europe with the development and production of technical zinc parts where the demands on precision, function and surface are high. Our experience with zinc die casting makes us a strong partner when the part is difficult and the solution has to perform reliably in series production. We even deliver to customers as far away as China.

At Linimatic we bring the decisive processes up to surface treatment together under one roof. This gives control over quality, process, delivery and documentation from the first sample to the finished part in zinc. Subsequent processes and surface treatment are carried out in close collaboration with fixed, specialised subcontractors.
Our customers choose Linimatic when they need high-pressure die-cast zinc parts with Danish production, high quality and competitive prices.
The best at the most difficult is not just a slogan. It is the way we work with zinc die casting.

certifications.detail: Certified since 1993 — over 30 years of independently audited quality management. Covers the complete value chain from incoming material through casting, machining, surface treatment, assembly, and final inspection.

certifications.name: Environmental Compliance
certifications.detail: Compliant with EU environmental regulations including REACH and RoHS. Active waste reduction and energy management programmes. Zinc scrap is recycled directly in production with near-zero material waste.

certifications.name: Material Certifications
certifications.detail: Full material traceability on all Zamak alloys. Incoming material certificates verified against specification. Batch-level traceability from raw material through to finished component.

sustainability.p1: Zinc is infinitely recyclable. At Linimatic, virtually all casting scrap — runners, overflows, and reject parts — is remelted and fed back into production. Our closed-loop recycling means near-zero zinc waste leaves the facility. The low melting point of zinc (385°C vs. 660°C for aluminium) translates directly to lower energy consumption per casting cycle.
sustainability.p2: We invest in energy-efficient equipment, LED facility lighting, and heat recovery systems. Our lead-free Zinkers product line demonstrates that environmental responsibility and product performance are not trade-offs. For procurement teams with sustainability reporting requirements, we provide verified data on recycling rates, energy consumption, and waste metrics.

zink-temadag-september-2026.title: Zinc Info Day on 16 September 2026
zink-temadag-september-2026.excerpt: A free info day on zinc die-casting at Linimatic in Helsinge — from material choice and design to production and finished part.
body: On 16 September 2026 we open the doors to our production in Helsinge for a free info day on zinc die-casting. The day lasts around four hours and is aimed at design engineers, project managers and buyers who want to know more about what zinc can do.

The programme covers the whole ground: zinc as a material and where it comes from, a comparison with aluminium and plastic, the casting process itself, designing in zinc with the possibilities and limits that brings, CO2 footprint, surface treatment, casting tools and the options for prototypes. Along the way there is a guided tour of the production, so you see the machines at work.
Feel free to bring a potential component or a specific problem — we will go through it on the day. The programme is always adapted to the participants.
Registration and questions: Jan V. Jørgensen, jaj@linimatic.dk or +45 2343 3667.

supplier-proximity.metaTitle: Ditlev Burke — a handle brought home from Asia
supplier-proximity.title: There are benefits to having your supplier close by
supplier-proximity.metric: It is possible to compete with Asia · Automated die-casting in Denmark
supplier-proximity.overview: Linimatic A/S is seeing growing demand from customers who want to bring production of zinc die-cast parts home to Denmark. Ditlev Burke Industrial Tools A/S in Asnæs is one of them: a handle for professional tools now contains a zinc part from Linimatic, and the entire handle is assembled in Denmark instead of Asia.
supplier-proximity.challenge: "We are incredibly happy with the projects we have run in collaboration with Linimatic A/S. Most recently, we have collaborated on a new handle containing a zinc part manufactured by Linimatic. The result is that we can now manufacture the plastic part and pre-assemble it ourselves, so that the entire handle is manufactured in Denmark rather than as before in Asia," said Camilla Burke Vedsmand, Managing Director at Ditlev Burke Industrial Tools A/S, located in Asnæs on Zealand.
supplier-proximity.approach: "When, as with Linimatic, you have an automated production line, we have from our own experience been able to establish that it is possible to compete with Asia," said Camilla Burke Vedsmand. Among other obvious benefits of the partnership, she mentioned the close cooperation, the quality and the reliability: "Communication within the country's borders is just so much faster, and therefore ensures progress in the projects. This has been a significant motivation in developing the long-term collaboration with Linimatic in North Zealand." "It is important for us that we have the same uniform understanding and approach to the tasks. Linimatic A/S are extremely skilled technically, and we are particularly pleased that the collaboration also supports our philosophy of retaining jobs in Denmark," she added.
supplier-proximity.result: The entire handle is now manufactured in Denmark instead of in Asia.

velux-kanban.metaTitle: VELUX — forecast agreement and robot automation
velux-kanban.title: Smooth collaboration with a forecast agreement
velux-kanban.metric: Forecast agreement renewed annually · Robot introduced on the production line
velux-kanban.overview: VELUX's Gåsdal division has run on a standing Kanban and forecast agreement with Linimatic for several years, making the collaboration easier and more predictable for both sides. The agreement is renewed every year, includes built-in price protection against raw material and currency swings — and has, among other things, led to a robot now handling the parts in production.
velux-kanban.challenge: "Of course there's a price agreement with built-in protection for both parties, for example against fluctuations in raw material prices and exchange rates. But perhaps even more importantly, the agreement also lets Linimatic plan and adjust production capacity, and so be able to deliver quickly, at the agreed quality and the agreed time," says Lars Daugaard Pedersen, strategic purchaser at VELUX.
velux-kanban.approach: "We're of course always looking for savings, and we talked to Linimatic about ways to shave a bit off the price. Linimatic suggested implementing a robot on the production line. We didn't have to pay for the robot itself, just a small investment in a special gripper adapted to our parts. With the robot, we now save the wage cost of the operator who used to handle our part, and the result is a solid saving," explains Lars Daugaard Pedersen. "Things just run — and a clear advantage is that we don't have to negotiate all the time. We have really good sparring with Linimatic's technicians, and there's always room to bring a new idea to the table."
velux-kanban.result: A close, smooth collaboration for both parties — no constant renegotiation, with ongoing sparring and knowledge-sharing between Linimatic and VELUX.

frandsen-downlight.metaTitle: Frandsen — from China to Denmark on short notice
frandsen-downlight.title: Faster, smarter - and made in Denmark
frandsen-downlight.metric: Reshored from China to Denmark under time pressure · Cast in a single process
frandsen-downlight.overview: Frandsen was ready to deliver downlight lamps to the international design company Concrete for the US market when its Chinese supplier pulled out just before production was due to start. Linimatic redesigned the parts for zinc die-casting and got the process running on very short notice — cast in a single step instead of multiple tooling stages, with extra weekend shifts to hold the schedule.
frandsen-downlight.challenge: "We had very little time to find an alternative. It looked really difficult. But when we contacted Linimatic and told Torben about the project, he just said: 'No problem, we'll make it happen!' And he said it so calmly. And they did it — we were honestly very surprised at how well it worked out," says Andreas Olesen, design engineer at Frandsen Project.
frandsen-downlight.approach: "It really was an extremely fast process — I have to admit I didn't quite believe it myself. One of the advantages was that the lamps could be cast in a single process, which saved time. So all in all, we got a smoother, faster process — and a smarter product, made right here in Denmark," explains Andreas Olesen. "The fast process is definitely unique for this project. A schedule was set, and only small slips were allowed to stay on track. And the few things that did slip, Linimatic handled with a weekend shift and extreme flexibility. It's very clear that they're skilled at project management — a really positive experience for us on this project. You know exactly how long everything takes — they control the processes 100%."
frandsen-downlight.result: The lamps were delivered on time for the US market launch, made in Denmark instead of China — and Frandsen now increasingly turns to Linimatic for more projects.

one-collection-finn-juhl.metaTitle: One Collection — the Finn Juhl table relaunched in die-cast zinc
one-collection-finn-juhl.title: To relaunch a classic design
one-collection-finn-juhl.metric: Finn Juhl logo cast directly into the fitting · Exhibited at the Milan design fair, 2015
one-collection-finn-juhl.overview: When furniture company One Collection decided to relaunch Finn Juhl's classic dining table with an advanced pull-out leaf, Linimatic was brought in to manufacture the precise fittings that carry the leaves. The leaves had to both hang and lie in a very specific way — and the fittings are both a technical function and a visible part of the iconic design.
one-collection-finn-juhl.challenge: "Fittings are often a necessary evil. But at Finn Juhl the fittings have a technical function, and they're also part of the visual design. That creates particular challenges for manufacturers. The simpler things look, the more complicated they can be to make. That's actually what we experienced," says Henrik Sørensen, CEO of One Collection.
one-collection-finn-juhl.approach: "By making the fittings in die-cast zinc, we could get the visual expression we wanted — while also having a high degree of precision. It was also possible to cast the Finn Juhl logo directly during the casting process, saving us a work step," says Henrik Sørensen, continuing: "The collaboration throughout the process is very much a dialogue. Linimatic has skills we don't have, and they were brought in. It's also important to feel engagement, passion — that the supplier also finds the product interesting."
one-collection-finn-juhl.result: The new Finn Juhl 'Nyhavn' dining table (model FJ 5360) launched with the precision-cast zinc fittings — with the Finn Juhl logo cast directly into the fitting — and was exhibited at the Milan design fair on 13 April 2015.

prototyping.title: Prototyping in Zinc
prototyping.overview:
In some projects, it can be an advantage to produce prototypes in zinc before investing in the final production tooling. The prototypes can be made by combining cast zinc with subsequent CNC machining.

This makes it possible to test function, assembly, fit, and appearance in the actual material. We assess together with the customer whether the method is relevant, and manage the whole process from initial clarification to finished prototypes.
prototyping.processHeading: How we make your zinc prototype

process.description: Together with you, we assess whether zinc prototyping is the right method for your project, and agree on scope and timeline.
Small, specially made zinc blocks are cast, suited for the subsequent CNC machining.
The cast zinc blocks are CNC-machined into finished prototypes, precisely to your drawings and specifications.
The finished prototype is delivered ready for testing function, assembly, fit, and appearance in the actual material. Typical turnaround is 2-4 weeks.

prototyping.advantagesHeading: Why prototype with your production foundry

advantages.p1: In some cases, a zinc prototype can be a good and cost-effective way to validate your idea and confirm the material's suitability for your specific application — before you invest in the final production tool.

faq.question: How fast can I get a zinc prototype?
faq.answer: It depends on the part's complexity and the amount of CNC machining involved. Contact us with your timeline, and we'll get back to you with a concrete estimate of feasibility and lead time.

faq.question: How are casting and CNC machining combined in a prototype?
faq.answer: Small, specially made zinc blocks are cast, suited for the subsequent CNC machining.

prototyping.ctaDescription: Contact us, and we’ll assess together whether zinc prototyping is the right solution for your project — with honest feedback on process, timeline, and price.

dieCasting.title: High-Pressure Die Casting
dieCasting.overview: High-pressure die casting is at the core of everything we do. At our foundry in Helsinge, 9 robotized casting cells run around the clock, producing zinc parts from 1 gram to 4 kilos — from small precision components to large, complex parts. The process is monitored continuously, so quality stays the same from the first shot to the last. With as-cast tolerances down to ±0.05 mm, many parts can be used without any secondary machining. That makes us Denmark’s largest dedicated zinc die-casting foundry — and the natural choice when the part is difficult and the requirements are high.
dieCasting.processHeading: From molten alloy to finished casting

process.description: The Zamak alloy is kept molten in the machine’s integrated furnace at a tightly controlled temperature. The zinc is forced directly from the furnace into the die tool — fully controlled and automated, in one closed system, with no manual handling. The result is faster casting cycles and consistent quality, shot after shot.
Molten zinc is injected into the hardened die tool at pressures up to 200 MPa. Fill times under 50 ms ensure optimal cavity fill even in thin-walled and complex geometries, with minimal porosity.

Parts are extracted by robotic arms within seconds of solidification. Runners and overflows are separated from the part and either returned immediately to the furnace or remelted for reuse — helping keep the CO2 footprint low.

Process verification is carried out according to the requirements agreed with the customer at the quotation stage. CMM spot-check inspections and SPC data (statistical process control) are used to ensure the process remains stable.

dieCasting.advantagesHeading: Why Linimatic is the best for the most complex

advantages.p1: Our 9 robotized casting cells cover the full tonnage range from 20T for small precision components to 315T for large structural parts — all with robotic handling. That singular focus gives us the deep process knowledge it takes to cast complex parts.
advantages.p2: Our experience with casting process simulation is rare in the industry. We simulate fill, solidification, and porosity before the tool is even built, so we get an optimized die from the very first shot. That lets us cast highly complex products where others have to give up. The same experience makes us a natural choice for high-end products and other demanding projects — including complex solutions for casting other metal components directly into the part during the die-casting process, where tolerances and material interaction have to be precisely matched.
advantages.p3: Many of our customers’ parts move on to surface treatment and a thorough visual final inspection before they’re ready for use. We have years of experience with this — from choosing the right post-treatment to the final check of appearance and finish before the part leaves the building.

faq.question: What is high-pressure die casting?
faq.answer: Hot-chamber die casting of zinc is a fast and precise process in which molten zinc at 420°C is injected into a die tool under high pressure. The method is especially suited to series production of complex parts with tight tolerances, thin wall sections, and a fine surface finish.

faq.question: Which Zamak alloy should I use?
faq.answer: About 95% of the parts we cast use Zamak 5, our standard alloy — a strong, well-rounded balance of strength, ductility, and castability (331 MPa tensile strength). The remaining 5% we cast in Zamak 8, which we use when Zamak 5’s strength isn’t sufficient — it’s the strongest and most creep-resistant zinc alloy we cast (374 MPa). Beyond that, we can also cast in Zamak 2, which offers the highest hardness and suits bearing surfaces, or Zamak 3, which has the best plating characteristics. We advise on the right choice during the DFM review of your drawing.

faq.question: What part sizes can you cast?
faq.answer: We cast parts from 1 g to 4 kg across our 9 casting cells. The optimal machine is selected based on part weight, projected area, and the required clamping force. The number of cavities is determined by the requirements for quality, complexity, and efficiency.

faq.question: How long does a zinc die-casting tool last?
faq.answer: Zinc die-casting tools routinely exceed 1 million shots — 5 to 10 times longer than aluminium die-casting tools. This is because zinc’s lower casting temperature (385°C vs. 660°C for aluminium) creates significantly less thermal stress on the die steel. All tools are maintained under our preventive maintenance programme.

faq.question: What tolerances can zinc die casting achieve?
faq.answer: As-cast tolerances to ±0.05 mm are standard on our machines. For features requiring tighter control, secondary CNC machining can achieve even higher precision. We publish tolerance recommendations by feature type (linear, bore, flatness) during DFM review.

dieCasting.ctaDescription: Send us your part drawing and volume requirements. We’ll recommend the right alloy, estimate tooling cost, and provide a piece price — within 48 hours.

postProcessing.title: CNC Post-Processing
postProcessing.overview: While zinc die casting offers great scope for casting very tight tolerances directly in the casting process, some parts require post-machining to achieve the desired tolerance on surfaces, holes, and milled threads. That is why CNC machining has been one of our in-house processes for more than 20 years: parts go from casting to finished, inspected component without leaving the building — and without external suppliers along the way. Our machining centre handles milling, drilling, thread cutting and thread milling — all under the same roof as the casting.
postProcessing.processHeading: The production flow — from quotation to finished part

process.description: Process planning starts as early as the quotation stage. Planning the entire production flow when we prepare the quotation is the foundation for the most efficient production process possible.
Multi-axis CNC milling centres machine critical features: bores, threads, mating surfaces, and tight-tolerance dimensions that exceed as-cast capability.

After casting and CNC machining, the various deburring processes come into play. The process is chosen to match the customer's surface requirements: vibratory deburring, shot blasting, plastic media blasting, or tumbling.

Process verification is carried out according to the requirements agreed with the customer at the quotation stage. CMM spot-check inspections and SPC data (statistical process control) are used to ensure the process remains stable.

advantages.p1: When casting, CNC machining, and deburring all happen under one roof, there is one supplier and one responsibility throughout. No coordination between foundry and machine shop, no transport between suppliers — and no quality gaps between steps. Parts move from casting to machining in hours instead of weeks.

faq.question: Do zinc die-cast parts need machining?
faq.answer: Not always. Many features can be cast to final tolerance (±0.05 mm as-cast). However, machining is typically required for threaded holes, precision bores, critical mating surfaces, or any feature where the design tolerance is tighter than what the casting process can reliably achieve.

faq.question: Can you mill threads in die-cast zinc parts?
faq.answer: Yes. Threaded holes and milled threads are produced as part of our in-house CNC post-processing. Because machining takes place in the same building and under the same quality system as casting, you get high precision and stable quality.

faq.question: What tolerances can secondary machining achieve?
faq.answer: Secondary CNC machining on zinc die-cast parts can achieve tolerances significantly tighter than the ±0.05 mm as-cast standard. The achievable tolerance depends on the specific feature type, part geometry, and fixturing. We specify achievable tolerances during DFM review.

faq.question: What deburring methods do you use?
faq.answer: We use vibratory deburring, shot blasting, plastic media blasting, and tumbling. The process is chosen based on the customer's surface requirements and the geometry of the part.

postProcessing.ctaDescription: Tell us which features need tighter tolerances and we’ll plan the machining strategy alongside the die design — before any steel is cut.

surfaceTreatment.title: Surface Treatment & Coating
surfaceTreatment.overview:
Zinc lends itself well to a wide range of surface treatments, where function, durability and visual appearance can all be tailored to the finished product. At Linimatic we work with experienced surface-treatment specialists in both Denmark and abroad, so we can offer solutions that match your requirements for finish, corrosion protection and application.

Surface treatment can give zinc parts a strong visual appearance, increase durability and protect against corrosion. This makes high-pressure die-cast, surface-treated zinc parts well suited to many different segments, including industry, technical components, furniture, interiors, design and the construction industry.
surfaceTreatment.processHeading: From raw casting to finished surface

process.step: Zinc – ideal for demanding surface treatment
process.description: High-pressure die-cast zinc parts are well suited to many types of surface treatment, making them a strong choice for technical components with high demands on function and finish. At Linimatic A/S we produce precision die-cast zinc components that, after proper pre-treatment, can be finished with chromate/passivation, Chrome III, powder coating, wet painting and electroplated coatings, among others. The dense structure and good dimensional stability of zinc provide a solid basis for adhesion, corrosion protection and a uniform visual appearance.

We help you choose the right surface finish based on your wishes and requirements for the surface. Multi-layer treatment is often necessary on zinc (e.g. copper-nickel-chrome) when it comes to the highest cosmetic standards.

During the surface treatment, process-specific requirements for temperature, layer thickness and curing time are followed. The process is continuously monitored and documented, including measurement of coating thickness, to ensure consistent and stable quality across production batches.

Finished surface-treated products with special finish requirements are, as a rule, subject to 100% visual inspection at Linimatic before delivery. This ensures that the products meet the agreed quality and the desired visual appearance.

specs.label: Protective and decorative – full RAL range

surfaceTreatment.advantagesHeading: Surface treatment starts with the casting itself

advantages.p1: Linimatic knows the part, the material and the requirements from the casting process itself. That means we can ensure that design, casting, pre-treatment and surface treatment are all aligned with one another. We coordinate the surface treatment with carefully selected and approved subcontractors, and carry out the final quality control and packing at Linimatic. That gives you a single, complete delivery and one accountable partner.

faq.question: What surface treatments can be applied to die-cast zinc?
faq.answer: Die-cast zinc parts can be powder coated, wet painted, chrome plated, nickel plated and passivated, among other options. Before final treatment, parts can be tumbled, vibratory deburred, bead blasted or shot blasted to achieve the desired surface texture.

faq.question: How do we choose the right surface treatment?
faq.answer: The choice depends on requirements for appearance, corrosion resistance, wear resistance and price. It also matters whether the part will be used indoors or outdoors, and whether it will be exposed to moisture, chemicals or mechanical wear. Linimatic is happy to help find the solution that suits both function and budget.

faq.question: Is surface treatment always necessary?
faq.answer: No. For certain indoor or hidden components, die-cast zinc can be used without further surface treatment. Treatment is typically chosen when there are specific requirements for appearance, corrosion protection, wear resistance or ease of cleaning.

faq.question: Can die-cast zinc be powder coated?
faq.answer: Yes. Die-cast zinc parts can be powder coated in a wide range of colours and surface textures. The part's design, casting quality, pre-treatment and curing temperature all affect the final result, so powder coating requirements should be considered as early as the design phase.

faq.question: Can zinc parts be chrome or nickel plated?
faq.answer: Yes. Die-cast zinc is well suited to electroplated coatings such as copper, nickel and chrome. These treatments can provide both a decorative appearance and functional protection. A good result requires a controlled casting process, proper pre-treatment and a part design suited to the treatment.

faq.question: Can surface treatment hide marks and unevenness?
faq.answer: Only to a limited extent. A bright or high-gloss coating can actually make small imperfections more visible. High cosmetic requirements therefore need to be considered in the part's design, the die, the casting process and the mechanical pre-treatment.

faq.question: Does the part need to be specially designed for surface treatment?
faq.answer: It can be a major advantage. Hanging points, contact surfaces, threads, tolerances, drainage of process fluids, and areas that must not be coated should be clarified early on. Early dialogue can prevent problems and reduce the need for rework.

faq.question: Can Linimatic deliver parts fully surface-treated?
faq.answer: Yes. Linimatic manages the entire process, from casting and in-house post-processing to the desired external surface treatment. The coating itself is carried out by carefully selected and approved subcontractors. Final quality control and packing are done at Linimatic, so the customer receives a complete, delivery-ready solution.

surfaceTreatment.ctaDescription: Tell us your surface requirements — decorative, functional, or both — and we’ll recommend the right treatment for your application and volume.

quality.title: Quality & Certification
quality.eyebrow: More than 30 years of certified quality management
quality.overview: Linimatic has been ISO 9001 certified since 1993. Our quality management system forms the framework for all our business processes – from reviewing customer requirements and specifications to purchasing, incoming goods, production, quality control and delivery. All processes are carried out according to defined procedures and control plans, so quality is managed and documented throughout the entire process.
quality.processHeading: How we ensure quality at every step

process.description: Material certificates are checked upon receipt of the zinc.
Production is monitored continuously according to the defined control plan for each process.
Operators' self-inspection is supplemented by sample checks carried out by the quality department.
When agreed, SPC is used for ongoing measurement and documentation of process stability.
Critical dimensions and geometric tolerances are checked on a coordinate measuring machine (CMM) when specified.

quality.advantagesHeading: What does ISO 9001 mean for you as a customer?

advantages.p1: A certified quality management system gives you assurance that requirements, specifications and changes are handled systematically throughout the entire process. Deviations are recorded, the root cause investigated, and corrective actions carried out – reducing the risk of recurrence.
advantages.p2: In short, it means greater delivery reliability, fewer quality issues, and more predictable production.

faq.question: What quality certifications does Linimatic hold?
faq.answer: Linimatic has been ISO 9001 certified since 1993 — over 30 years of uninterrupted, independently audited quality management. The certification covers the complete value chain: incoming material inspection, die-casting, CNC machining, surface treatment, assembly, and final inspection.

faq.question: Can you provide PPAP documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. We provide PPAP documentation at Level 1 to 3 by agreement with the customer.

faq.question: How does Linimatic ensure quality during ongoing production?
faq.answer: Quality is monitored throughout production according to a defined control plan for each component and process. Operators’ ongoing self-inspection is supplemented by sample checks from the quality department. When agreed, SPC measurements are also used to monitor process stability, along with inspection on a coordinate measuring machine.

faq.question: What traceability do you provide per batch?
faq.answer: Every batch is traceable from raw material (alloy heat number, supplier certificate) through casting (machine, die, date, shift, process parameters) to machining, coating, inspection, and shipment.

quality.ctaHeading: Need to audit our quality system?
quality.ctaDescription: We welcome customer audits and facility visits. Contact us to schedule a quality review or request our current ISO certificate and capability documentation.

assembly.title: Assembly & Mounting
assembly.overview:

Among other things, we can handle assembly kits, spare-parts kits and smaller subsystems, as well as quality control, labelling, packing and customer-specific packaging.

By consolidating several processes with one supplier, you get simpler logistics, fewer handling steps and a more efficient supply chain.

Contact us to hear how we can create value through assembly and mounting.
assembly.processHeading: From component to fully assembled unit

process.description: We receive die-cast zinc components and other parts to be built into the finished unit.
The parts are assembled into fully assembled units — such as assembly kits, spare-parts kits or smaller subsystems.
Customer-specific packaging and labelling, tailored to your needs.
Quality control before delivery, ready for use or further delivery.

codeOfConductPage.title: Code of Conduct
intro: Vendor responsibility in social and sustainable entrepreneurship is central to the worldwide community and also plays an increasing role in a company's competitiveness and profitability.

Linimatic's Code of Conduct was established in 2021 to support this social and sustainable entrepreneurship, especially in the following areas: human rights; occupational health & labour issues; environmental management; and anti-corruption measures.
Linimatic has based its Code of Conduct on the UN Global Compact, an international initiative supported by businesses around the world with the aim of ensuring compliance in the aforementioned areas.
purpose: In order to respect human rights and to promote fair employment, safe working conditions, and responsible environmental and ethical standards, this Code of Conduct is applied in the production, supply, and delivery of all Linimatic's products and services.

In addition to all applicable laws, rules, and standards in the countries where Linimatic operates, all employees must comply with Linimatic's Code of Conduct — even where these requirements are more stringent than national laws and regulations.
Linimatic actively supports its suppliers in securing long-term, continuous improvements. Linimatic supports the UN's "Global Compact".
To make this commitment clear to employees, suppliers, customers, and other stakeholders, our Code of Conduct is based on the Global Compact's ten principles and is made public.
codeOfConductPage.freedomOfAssociationText: As far as applicable laws permit, all employees are free to form and be a member of — or not be a member of — trade unions or similar external unions, and to bargain collectively.
codeOfConductPage.forcedLaborText: Forced or compulsory work is expressly forbidden, and all employees are free to terminate their employment after reasonable notice in accordance with national law and/or prior agreement. Employees are not required to deposit money or identity papers with their employer.
codeOfConductPage.termsOfEmploymentText: Employees can expect that their employment rights, pay, and conditions are fair and reasonable, and meet, as a minimum, national legal requirements and industry standards. Working hours are in accordance with national law and are not abusive.
codeOfConductPage.accessToDataText: All employees have the right, at any time, to access their personal documents and information held by the company, in accordance with applicable data protection laws (GDPR). Requests for access should be directed to the company's HR department.
childLabour: No person employed is below the legal minimum age for employment. The minimum age is the age for completion of compulsory schooling, or a minimum of 15 years, in accordance with Article 2.4 of ILO Convention No. 138 on minimum age. Children are not hired for dangerous work, or for work that is not consistent with the child's personal development.

A child is a person under 18 years, as defined in Article 1 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. Personal development includes a child's health, or physical, mental, spiritual, moral, or social development, as described in Article 32 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.
discrimination: Employees are treated with respect and dignity. Corporal punishment, physical, verbal, or other unlawful harassment, and any form of threat or intimidation, is prohibited. All forms of discrimination based on bias or prejudice are prohibited, such as discrimination based on race, colour, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy, parental status, religion, political opinion, nationality, ethnic background, social origin, social status, disability, age, union membership, or any other characteristic or status protected by applicable local law.
Employees with the same qualifications, experience, and accomplishments receive equal pay for equal work with others who do the same work under similar working conditions.
workEnvironment: A healthy and safe working environment and, if applicable, housing provided for employees, is in accordance with international standards and national laws. Appropriate information and training on health and safety is provided for employees.

Security also includes compliance with national laws and regulations regarding fire prevention, as well as plans for evacuation in case of fire, at least as required by the national legislation in force at any given time. Safe and proper handling and labelling of chemicals, mechanical equipment, and work processes is handled in accordance with national legislation. Workplaces, and if applicable housing, have acceptable temperature and noise levels, adequate ventilation, adequate lighting, clean toilets, clean drinking water, and, if appropriate, sanitary facilities for food storage.
codeOfConductPage.environmentText: Finite resources are used responsibly and with caution. Approaches and methods that reduce any environmental impact linked to our business are welcomed. Innovative development of products and services that provide environmental and social benefits is promoted.
antiCorruption: No form of extortion or bribery, including improper offers of payment to or from employees, business relations, or organisations, is tolerated.

We are committed to conducting our business in alignment with applicable national and international competition laws, and we adhere to antitrust regulations, maintain robust data protection, and prioritise information security to safeguard sensitive information.
We are dedicated to preventing money laundering and avoiding the financing of terrorism.
codeOfConductPage.supplierSupplementHeading: Code of Conduct — Supplement for Suppliers
codeOfConductPage.supplierSupplementText: This Code of Conduct ("CODE") applies to all activities of Linimatic and to mutually contributing products, services, and activities from other businesses ("Suppliers").
codeOfConductPage.adherenceText: Linimatic requires that the supplier and its subcontractors meet the requirements of this Code of Conduct ("CODE"), which may mean more stringent requirements than the applicable national law. A supplier shall, upon request, reasonably verify that it and its subcontractors comply with the CODE. This can be done by providing information and/or allowing Linimatic or one of our representatives access to the site(s) of the aforementioned supplier/subcontractor.
codeOfConductPage.notificationText: The supplier is responsible for ensuring that its employees and subcontractors are informed of this Code of Conduct ("CODE") and that they meet the requirements contained therein.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.dataControllerIntro: Linimatic A/S is the data controller for personal data processed through this website and when you contact us.
privacyPage.whatWeCollectIntro: We may collect the following personal data through our website:
collectItems: Contact form submissions: Name, company, email address, phone number, enquiry subject, expected production volume and project description.
Job applications: Name, contact details, CV, cover letter, and other information you include in an application sent by email.

Technical and security data: Our hosting provider receives the form request and processes technical request data, such as IP address and browser information, to deliver and protect the website. The contact form uses a short-lived in-memory IP limit to prevent abuse; we do not store submissions in a website database.
Optional analytics: If you consent, Vercel Analytics processes cookieless visit measurements so we can understand which pages are useful. It is not loaded when you decline.
Communication data: Records of correspondence if you contact us by email or phone.
privacyPage.dataSourceNote: The form requires your name, company, email address and message so we can identify and answer your enquiry; phone number, subject and expected volume are optional. If a required field is omitted, the form cannot be submitted. Information in forms and emails comes from you. Some technical information, such as IP address and browser information, is generated automatically when you use the website.
privacyPage.legalBasisIntro: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), we process personal data based on:
legalBasisItems: Legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)): To receive and answer enquiries, assess applications, prevent abuse, and keep the website and our communication secure.
Pre-contractual steps (Art. 6(1)(b)): Where an enquiry leads to a request to prepare or enter into a contract.
Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)): Where a law requires us to retain or process information.
howWeUseItems: To respond to quote requests and customer inquiries
To prevent abuse and protect the security of the website and our communication
To understand which pages are useful when you have consented to analytics
To comply with legal and regulatory obligations
privacyPage.retentionIntro: We retain personal data only as long as necessary for the purposes described above, or as required by law. Specifically:
retentionItems: Contact enquiries: Normally reviewed and deleted from our mailboxes and related copies 2 years after the last contact. If an active business relationship or legal need requires longer retention, we keep only what is necessary and record the reason.
Job applications: Normally deleted 6 months after the position is filled, or 6 months after receipt or last contact for unsolicited applications, unless you consent to longer retention.
Security data: IP information used for the contact form's short-lived flood protection is kept in application memory, not in a contact database.
Analytics data: Collected only after consent and described as cookieless and anonymized by Vercel; see our Cookie Policy.
privacyPage.dataSharingIntro: We do not sell your personal data. We may share data with:
dataSharingItems: Vercel (hosting and form runtime): Hosts the website and runs the server-side contact form. It may process the submitted form data and technical request metadata as part of providing the service. Vercel is a US company and processing may take place in the US and other countries under the applicable service terms and safeguards.

Resend (email delivery): Delivers contact form messages, including the visitor's contact details, message, reply address, and related email metadata. Resend states that its primary processing operations take place in the United States; choosing an Ireland sending region does not make customer data EU-only. Transfers are covered by Resend's Data Processing Addendum and the safeguards described there.

Microsoft 365 (email and collaboration): Hosts our email accounts, where contact-form enquiries, job applications and other correspondence are received and stored. Data is held within the EU/EFTA region.
Legal authorities: When required by law or to protect our rights.
privacyPage.dataSharingDpaNote: For the providers' detailed data-processing terms, see the <vercel>Vercel Data Processing Addendum</vercel> and <resend>Resend Data Processing Addendum</resend>.
privacyPage.dataSharingNote: We use providers only where needed to run the website and handle enquiries. Before publication and when a provider changes, we verify the provider's agreement, processing locations, sub-processors and retention in our internal processor register. Where personal data is transferred outside the EU/EEA, the applicable provider agreement and a valid GDPR transfer mechanism, such as Standard Contractual Clauses, are used where required.
privacyPage.yourRightsIntro: Under GDPR, you have the right to:
yourRightsItems: Access — Request a copy of the personal data we hold about you.
Rectification — Request correction of inaccurate data.
Erasure — Request deletion of your data (“right to be forgotten”).
Restriction — Request limitation of data processing.
Portability — Request your data in a structured, machine-readable format.
Objection — Object to processing based on legitimate interest.
Withdraw consent — Withdraw previously given consent at any time.
privacyPage.yourRightsContact: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at linimatic@linimatic.dk. We will respond within one month, unless a lawful extension applies.
privacyPage.complaintsText: If you believe your data protection rights have been violated, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Danish Data Protection Agency (Datatilsynet):
privacyPage.changesText: We may update this privacy policy from time to time. The “last updated” date at the top reflects the most recent revision. We encourage you to review this page periodically.

cookiePolicyPage.title: Cookie Policy
cookiePolicyPage.whatAreCookiesText: Cookies are small text files placed on your device when you visit a website. They are widely used to make websites work more efficiently and provide information to website owners. Under EU regulation (the ePrivacy Directive and GDPR), we are required to obtain your consent before placing non-essential cookies.
cookiePolicyPage.howWeUseText: We use two categories: necessary, which is always on, and analytics, which we only use if you agree. We use no cookies for marketing and share no data with advertising networks. You can change your choice at any time via “Cookie settings” at the bottom of any page.
cookiePolicyPage.necessaryText: These cookies are essential for the website to function properly. They support basic website functions and remember your cookie preferences. The website cannot function properly without them, and they cannot be disabled.
cookiePolicyPage.popupStoragePurpose: Remembers that you closed the panel about our zinc info days, so it does not reappear straight away
cookiePolicyPage.storageNote: The last entry in the table is not a cookie but a note stored locally in your browser. It contains only a timestamp and is never sent to us or to anyone else.
cookiePolicyPage.analyticsText: If you agree to analytics, we load Vercel Analytics to measure page visits and understand which pages are useful. It is not loaded when you decline. Vercel describes the service as cookieless and anonymized; its own privacy information explains how it handles analytics data.
cookiePolicyPage.managingText1: When you first visit our website, a cookie banner will appear allowing you to accept all cookies, reject all non-essential cookies, or customize your preferences by category.
cookiePolicyPage.managingText2: You can change your choice or withdraw your consent at any time via the "Cookie settings" link at the bottom of every page.
cookiePolicyPage.managingText3: You can also control cookies through your browser settings. Most browsers allow you to refuse or delete cookies. The methods for doing so vary from browser to browser — consult your browser’s help documentation.
cookiePolicyPage.thirdPartyText: We use no advertising networks, social media buttons, maps or videos that set cookies on our pages, and fonts are served from our own server. Vercel hosts the website and runs the contact form; if you agree to analytics, it also measures visits. Resend delivers contact-form messages to our business email provider, which stores them in our Linimatic mailbox. These services may process data outside the EU/EEA as described in our Privacy Policy.
cookiePolicyPage.contactText: If you have questions about our use of cookies, contact us at:

zinkTemadagPage.heading: Zinc Die-Casting Info Day
zinkTemadagPage.intro:
Get practical knowledge about the possibilities of zinc die-casting – from material selection and design to production and the finished part.

Linimatic holds free info days for designers, project managers and buyers at our facility in Helsinge. Feel free to bring along a potential component or a specific challenge for us to go through on the day. See the agenda below.
agenda: Zinc in general — and where it comes from
Zinc compared to aluminum and plastic
Designing in zinc — possibilities and limitations
